evidence_quotes.quote: This paper analyzes cadastral updating and its impact on the strengthening of local institutional capacities, from the point of view of property tax collection for the provision of home public utilities of water and sewerage.

La unidad de análisis comprende los 53 municipios de los departamentos de Caldas, Quindío y Risaralda, como se muestra en la Figura 1; las observaciones se realizan en dos períodos que abarcan cinco años para cada periodo, divididos a partir del año de la actualización catastral.
librería Walrus – Robust Statistical Methods, basada en el trabajo de Mair & Wilcox (2020), y se aplicó la prueba Robust Paired Samples T-Test.
Los resultados de la Tabla 2 (p=0.05) permiten rechazar la hipótesis nula —con una d de Cohen superior al 0.80 que indica un efecto de magnitud alto— en 27 de los 53 municipios;

existe un aumento significativo en la cobertura de acueducto posterior a la actualización catastral, lo que corresponde al 15.15% de los municipios; mientras se acepta la hipótesis nula en el resto de los municipios, es decir, no existen diferencias significativas en el 84.85%.

En el servicio de alcantarillado, el aumento ha sido significativo en suscriptores y cobertura después de la actualización catastral en cerca del 67% de los municipios. El IRCA en el 69% de los municipios se mantiene sin cambios significativos, mientras que en el resto de municipios aumentó;

country.comment: Study analyzes 53 municipalities in the Colombian departments of Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda.
country.where_found: PDF p. 4, Introducción; PDF p. 6, Catastro y SGP; PDF p. 7, Metodología y Datos, Figura 1

effect_estimate.comment: Municipality-by-municipality Robust Paired Samples T-Tests comparing 5-year pre-update vs. 5-year post-update periods (alpha = 0.05). Note that for IRCA, p. 16 reports 71.43% (30/42) without significant differences while p. 17 summarizes this as 69%. Tables 2, 3, 4, and 7 display truncated row lists in the PDF layout, while the text reports full subsample totals.
effect_estimate.value: Across 53 municipalities comparing 5-year periods before vs. after cadastral updating via Robust Paired Samples T-Tests (p < 0.05): property tax revenue increased significantly in 27/53 municipalities (50.94%, Cohen's d > 0.80) and per capita property tax in 29/53 (54.72%, d > 0.69); central government SGP water/sanitation transfers increased significantly in 13/52 municipalities (25.0%, d > 0.81); aqueduct (water) subscribers increased significantly in 8/33 municipalities (24.24%, d > 0.77) and aqueduct proxy coverage in 5/33 (15.15%, d > 0.82; no significant change in 84.85%); sewerage subscribers increased significantly in 22/33 municipalities (66.67%, d > 0.56) and sewerage proxy coverage in 22/33 (66.67%, d > 0.56; no significant change in 33.33%); and the drinking water quality risk index (IRCA) increased significantly (indicating higher risk) in 12/42 municipalities (28.57%, d > 0.87), with no significant change in 30/42 (71.43%). Rural and urban cadastres had not been updated in the prior 17 years in 96% (51/53) and 98% of municipalities, respectively.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 8, Resultados; PDF pp. 9–15, Tables 2–7; PDF pp. 11, 16–17, Resultados and Conclusiones

mechanism_certainty.comment: Rated 1 (documented statistical association): the study documents pre-post statistical differences following municipal cadastral updates using secondary administrative series without an untreated control group (Serious/Critical confounding risk from concurrent municipal tax reforms, urban growth, and water-sampling changes) and without directly observing internal municipal budget allocation or utility connection processes.

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Non-randomized longitudinal pre-post (before-and-after) evaluation of a specific administrative intervention (municipal cadastral updating across staggered years 2004–2015), comparing 5-year pre-update vs. 5-year post-update periods within each municipality. Because it lacks a contemporaneous untreated comparator group or adjustment for secular trends and co-interventions, it carries Serious/Critical confounding risk under ROBINS-I.

sample_size.comment: Total sample is 53 municipalities, each compared across a 5-year pre-update period and a 5-year post-update period (10 years per municipality within 2000–2020); missing historical data in administrative platforms reduced subsamples for SGP transfers (52), subscribers/coverage (33), and IRCA (42).
sample_size.value: 53 municipalities across 3 departments (Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda) observed over two 5-year periods (10 years per municipality); outcome subsamples: 53 municipalities (property tax and per capita property tax), 52 municipalities (SGP water/sanitation transfers), 33 municipalities (aqueduct and sewerage subscribers and coverage), and 42 municipalities (IRCA water quality)

study_design.value: Quantitative longitudinal before-and-after (pre-post) municipal study comparing two 5-year periods (before vs. after cadastral updating) using Robust Paired Samples T-Tests
